memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "As they were emptying their sacks, there in each man's sack was his pouch of silver! When they and their father saw the money pouches, they were frightened" - Gen 42:35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the brothers empty their sacks at home, they make a startling discovery: every single man's silver has been returned. Not just one, but all of them find their money in their bags. And once again, the response is fear: "When they and their father saw the money pouches, they were frightened."

Here again is that strange reaction — an unexpected kindness met with dread rather than delight. The returned silver could have been seen as a gracious gift, but to hearts weighed down by guilt and fear, it looked like a threat, a mystery, a source of danger. Even Jacob, who did not share his sons' specific guilt, was caught up in the fear.

Fear, once it takes hold, tends to spread and to color everything. The brothers' fear became the whole family's fear. And fear has a way of interpreting even good news as bad, even blessing as threat. When we are gripped by anxiety, we lose the ability to see clearly; we expect the worst and read danger into every circumstance.

The remedy is to bring our fears to God and to remember His character. Much of what frightens us is not what it seems. The very silver that terrified this family was actually a sign of favor from the one person who could save them. When fear tells you that everything is against you, pause and remember that God is for you (Rom 8:31), and that His providences, even the puzzling ones, are working for your good.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Does fear cause you to read even good things as threats?
How does your anxiety spread and color everything around you?
Where do you need to remember that God is for you, not against you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when fear grips me and colors everything dark, help me to remember Your character. You are for me, not against me. Steady my heart, and help me to see Your hand rightly. Amen.
